items.title: PM owns the provider registry and provider projections are consumers
items.statement: The WebProviderAdapterRegistry is the single provider-capability authority; downstream provider, MCP, model-native, coding-agent, and GUI projections consume it and persist credential references rather than secrets.

evidence.exact_quote: - The WebProviderAdapterRegistry is the PM-owned single source of truth for web provider and adapter capability. Registry rows bind provider ID, adapter ID, adapter kind (`pm_native`, `direct_api`, `mcp_server`, `model_native`, `cli_bridge`, or `server_bridge`), operation capability, support tier, effective cost/cache policy, fallback rank, health state, robots behavior, egress policy, SSRF/private-host policy, credential reference, and projection state. Provider config files, MCP projections, model-native provider projections, coding-agent projections, and GUI settings rows are consumers of this registry, not competing sources of provider truth, and they must serialize credential references only, never raw secrets.

items.title: Dispatcher normalizes operation identity and validates before routing
items.statement: Every invocation maps to one canonical operation and is validated before adapter selection; malformed or unsupported inputs are not handed to providers.

evidence.exact_quote: - The web dispatcher maps each invocation to one canonical operation (`search`, `extract`, `research`, `deep_research`, `crawl`, `map`, or `fetch`/`read`), validates parameters against that operation's contract before adapter routing, and rejects malformed or unsupported inputs with `invalid_input` instead of handing them to a provider.

items.title: Research has bounded autonomous and deterministic composed branches
items.statement: Autonomous research may use provider-native behavior or a composed recipe and is capped at three search iterations, max_sources reads, and 120 seconds; the omitted-or-false branch deterministically searches, selects, reads up to auto_read_cap, and synthesizes without page interaction.

evidence.exact_quote: - When `autonomous: true` is set on `webresearch`, PM may use provider-native autonomous research when available; Firecrawl delegates to `/v2/agent`, Tavily uses its advanced search + extract chain, and other providers use the PM-composed enhanced recipe: search, read top pages through Site Reader, refine and repeat only when evidence is insufficient, then synthesize with citations. Autonomous research remains bounded to at most three search iterations, at most `max_sources` page reads, and a 120s total runtime unless a narrower provider or run limit applies; each step surfaces activity such as `Searching Web: <refined query>` and `Reading Site: <url>`.

- When `autonomous: false` or omitted on `webresearch`, the default PM-composed research recipe is deterministic and bounded: search with the highest-priority provider, select top candidate URLs up to `max_sources`, read/extract up to `auto_read_cap` pages via Site Reader as the auto-read cap, then synthesize an answer with citations from read content. In this branch the agent does NOT navigate or interact with pages; interaction-capable browser work must route through the explicit WebAction or browser/session contracts.

items.title: Web approvals are scoped by whether the target is known
items.statement: Discovery operations use wildcard-only approval, while operations with a known URL or site use host/site-scoped approval.

evidence.exact_quote: - Permission requests for `websearch` and `webresearch` are wildcard-only operation approvals because the URL set is not known before discovery, while `/extract/crawl/map` and `webfetch` use host/site-scoped approvals when their target is known.

items.title: Extraction failures and schema modes have explicit outcomes
items.statement: Empty extraction, oversized or invalid schemas, and strict-versus-lenient conformance are distinguished with concrete codes, output shapes, and warning/error behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - `extraction_empty` means extraction completed but produced no data because page content did not match the schema or prompt. Output includes `extracted_data: null` and `schema_conformance: "none"`; lenient mode treats this as a WARNING with empty data plus a warning, while strict mode treats it as an ERROR.

- Schema validation modes apply to `webextract` and schema-backed `webresearch`. In `"strict"` mode, output MUST conform to schema, non-conforming fields are dropped, and missing required fields return `extraction_schema_mismatch`; in `"lenient"` mode (default), output uses best-effort conformance, keeps non-conforming fields with `_schema_violation: true` annotation, and treats missing required fields as a warning, not an error.

items.title: Outputs and audit payloads have locked shared and operation-specific shapes
items.statement: The common result envelope is extended, not replaced, by operation-specific fields, while semantic audit operation names and tool IDs are explicitly mapped.

evidence.exact_quote: - Web operation outputs share a locked common result envelope: `success: boolean`, `web_operation`, `support_tier`, `execution_path`, `requested_adapter_id?`, `effective_adapter_id?`, `adapter_selection_reason?`, `projection_freshness?`, `projection_health?`, `provider_fallback_occurred: boolean`, `provider_fallback_summary?`, `source_count?: number`, `sources?: Array<{ title?, url, snippet?, provenance_badge? }>`, `warnings?: string[]`, `error_code?: string`, and `error_message?: string`.

- `web_operation` uses semantic audit values `search`, `extract`, `research`, `crawl`, `map`, and `read`; `read` maps to the canonical `webfetch` tool. Audit payloads use `read` as the semantic operation name, while the underlying tool invocation is `webfetch`, and consumers MUST map between these vocabularies.

items.title: Site Reader produces typed rendered-page evidence with iframe attribution
items.statement: Site Reader owns structured rendered-page reading, typed PageRepresentation output, bounded iframe discovery, and visible prompt-injection indicators for downstream reasoning.

evidence.exact_quote: The Site Reader renderer pipeline MUST build a structured `PageRepresentation` rather than returning an untyped page dump. It extracts the accessibility tree, layout bounds for relevant nodes, landmarks, headings, interactive elements, forms, content summary/full content according to the requested detail level, and optionally discovered/merged iframe content. The representation carries typed page structure, interactive elements, forms, errors, optional interactive summary, optional iframes, console/network refs, screenshot/PDF artifact refs when requested, redaction profile IDs, and visible prompt-injection chips so downstream agents can reason about the page before acting. Prompt-injection indicators are visible chips and audit fields, not hidden prompt text.

Site Reader iframe handling is read-target behavior, not inline visualizer sandboxing. During structured reading, PM recursively discovers nested iframes up to 3 levels deep, attempts cross-origin iframe content extraction only where browser security policy allows, gracefully skips blocked same-origin or X-Frame-Options cases with a warning, may use per-frame diagnostic sessions when the PM-managed native browser runtime is available, and merges iframe content into the parent `PageRepresentation` with source-frame attribution. Playwright and CDP are reference/fallback test-driver vocabulary only; they do not replace the PM-managed native browser runtime or become product terms.

items.title: webfetch URL, binary, cache, and change behavior is substantially locked
items.statement: webfetch normalizes and validates HTTP(S) targets, applies a 5 MB default, distinguishes supported images from unsupported binary media, and defines cache and change-tracking defaults.

evidence.exact_quote: - webfetch URL handling is locked: reject non-HTTP(S) schemes such as `file://`, `ftp://`, and `javascript:`, normalize before routing, default bare domains to https://, reject malformed URLs with invalid_input, and enforce a default 5 MB max_content_length unless configured otherwise.
- webfetch defaults `cache_policy` to `{ max_age_seconds: 14400, store: true }` and uses hash-based `change_tracking` with status values `new|same|changed|removed`.

items.title: LSP keeps rename approval and remains complementary
items.statement: The widened LSP surface retains rename as a write-like action requiring explicit pre-apply approval, complements context compilation, and does not depend on provider-native skill installation for MVP.

evidence.exact_quote: - `rename` with explicit approval before apply
- it complements, but does not replace, context bundling performed by the context compiler

items.title: chatsearch is project-scoped and secrets-scrubbed
items.statement: chatsearch has a typed input/output shape, a per-project index boundary, mandatory pre-persistence secrets scrubbing, and Context Lens integration.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Input:** `query: string`, optional `filters: { thread_id?, time_range? }`, `k?: number`.
- **Secrets policy:** Persisted chat index content MUST comply with PolicyRule:no_secrets_in_storage / INV-002 (mandatory strict secrets scrubbing before persistence).

items.title: Unsupported input error taxonomy conflicts
items.statement: The dispatcher rule assigns `invalid_input` to unsupported inputs, while an unsupported requested search source or category returns `unsupported_operation`; the boundary between these outcomes is not defined.
items.impact: Equivalent unsupported capability requests can produce different canonical error codes across adapters or implementations.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must decide whether unsupported source/category values are invalid parameters or valid parameters with unavailable capability.

evidence.exact_quote: - The web dispatcher maps each invocation to one canonical operation (`search`, `extract`, `research`, `deep_research`, `crawl`, `map`, or `fetch`/`read`), validates parameters against that operation's contract before adapter routing, and rejects malformed or unsupported inputs with `invalid_input` instead of handing them to a provider.
A requested source or category unsupported by the effective provider returns `unsupported_operation` for that source or category.

items.title: SSRF and private-host enforcement has no locked default behavior
items.statement: The registry stores an SSRF/private-host policy, but this core does not state the default policy, when DNS/IP revalidation occurs, redirect handling, or the denial code for a blocked private target.
items.impact: Provider adapters can diverge on private-network access and redirect-based SSRF protection.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent enforcement timing, defaults, redirect treatment, and failure mapping.

evidence.exact_quote: Registry rows bind provider ID, adapter ID, adapter kind (`pm_native`, `direct_api`, `mcp_server`, `model_native`, `cli_bridge`, or `server_bridge`), operation capability, support tier, effective cost/cache policy, fallback rank, health state, robots behavior, egress policy, SSRF/private-host policy, credential reference, and projection state.

- webfetch URL handling is locked: reject non-HTTP(S) schemes such as `file://`, `ftp://`, and `javascript:`, normalize before routing, default bare domains to https://, reject malformed URLs with invalid_input, and enforce a default 5 MB max_content_length unless configured otherwise.

items.title: webfetch required content conflicts with metadata-only binary results
items.statement: The operation-specific result contract says webfetch returns `content: string`, but unsupported binary media returns metadata only without downloading the body; the result envelope for that successful metadata-only case is not defined.
items.impact: Typed consumers cannot know whether content is absent, empty, optional, or paired with a failure code for metadata-only responses.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose whether `content` becomes optional, empty, or the response becomes unsuccessful.

evidence.exact_quote: `webfetch` returns `content: string`, `status?: number`, `formats_returned?: string[]`, `screenshot?`, `cache_state?`, and `change_status?` for the requested URL

Unsupported or `/large` binary media such as video, audio, or executables returns metadata only (`MIME type`, `content-length`, `URL`) without downloading the body, and non-text responses do not enter HTML-to-Markdown conversion.

items.title: Autonomous research route selection is discretionary
items.statement: With `autonomous: true`, PM may use provider-native autonomous research when available, but no deterministic rule selects provider-native execution versus PM-composed execution when both are available.
items.impact: Identical requests can take materially different paths, costs, evidence collection behavior, and latency.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must decide whether adapter hint, fallback rank, cost, health, or another criterion controls the branch.

evidence.exact_quote: - When `autonomous: true` is set on `webresearch`, PM may use provider-native autonomous research when available; Firecrawl delegates to `/v2/agent`, Tavily uses its advanced search + extract chain, and other providers use the PM-composed enhanced recipe: search, read top pages through Site Reader, refine and repeat only when evidence is insufficient, then synthesize with citations.

items.title: Robots behavior lacks an operation-level default and refusal contract
items.statement: Robots behavior is registry data and `respect_robots` is an explicit crawl input, but this core does not define its default, precedence against provider narrowing, or the warning/error/result representation when robots rules exclude pages.
items.impact: Crawl scope and compliance can vary by adapter for the same omitted input.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose the default and how exclusions are surfaced and counted.

evidence.exact_quote: - `webcrawl` preserves `change_tracking`, `dedup`, `respect_robots`, `formats`, and `include/exclude_paths` as explicit web-operation inputs; providers may narrow unsupported behavior only through structured warnings or capability disclosure.

items.title: Browser session states are named without transition semantics
items.statement: The persisted browser session fields enumerate collapsed, detached, background, and runtime-unavailable state plus remediation IDs, but legal transitions, transition triggers, and recovery completion behavior are not specified.
items.impact: GUI, runtime, and tests can disagree about session availability and remediation lifecycle.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must create the session state machine and define whether these states are exclusive or combinable.

evidence.exact_quote: Browser sessions persist `browser_session_id`, `show_when_possible`, collapsed/detached/background/runtime-unavailable state, Open/Watch availability, and `runtime_unavailable` remediation action IDs so GUI and testing surfaces can explain degraded browser evidence without inventing separate routing.

items.title: LSP read-operation support is recommendation-level
items.statement: The section says the LSP surface is widened, but labels its expanded read-operation set as recommended rather than required, leaving MVP conformance unclear.
items.impact: Implementations may ship different LSP capabilities while each claims conformance.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose which recommended operations are mandatory for MVP.

evidence.exact_quote: The `lsp` tool surface is widened beyond the minimal MVP read trio.

items.title: Context Lens muted-message handling permits observably different paths
items.statement: chatsearch may either exclude muted message IDs before returning results or annotate them for later dropping, with no required output annotation field or consumer behavior.
items.impact: Agents, audit logs, and context packers may observe different hit sets and shapes.
items.builder_discretion: Builders choose early exclusion or late filtering and must invent the annotation contract if choosing late filtering.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Context Lens integration:** When Context Lens mutes messages, chatsearch MUST exclude muted message_ids from results returned to the agent (or annotate them as excluded so the context packer can drop them).

items.title: chatsearch query limits and filter semantics are unspecified
items.statement: The input names `k` and `time_range` but provides no defaults, bounds, time-range grammar, empty-query behavior, or invalid-filter error mapping.
items.impact: Backends and callers can disagree on pagination, resource limits, and validation outcomes.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose limits, defaults, parsing, and errors.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Input:** `query: string`, optional `filters: { thread_id?, time_range? }`, `k?: number`.

items.title: WebAction lacks per-action required-field rules
items.statement: WebAction is declared to have exact required and optional fields, but the exposed field list makes selector, value, timeout, and description globally optional and does not say which action types require or forbid which fields.
items.impact: Validation and execution of click, type, navigate, select, wait, and other actions can diverge before provider routing.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent an action-by-field validation matrix and error behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - WebAction is a locked typed interface with an exact action enum, required and optional fields, hard timing limits, sequential execution, and invalid_input on unknown action types.
- `selector?: string`
- `value?: string`

items.title: detail_hint and detail_level ownership is ambiguous
items.statement: webextract defines `detail_hint`, while the shared field inventory and Site Reader behavior use `detail_level`; this core does not define whether they are distinct inputs, how one maps to the other, or which surface owns `detail_level`.
items.impact: Adapters and Site Reader can interpret extraction depth inconsistently.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must define the mapping and valid detail_level enum.

evidence.exact_quote: `webextract` accepts `url: string`, `adapter_hint?: string`, `detail_hint?: "fast" | "balanced" | "deep"` for provider/API-side (`/API-side`) extraction or PM-composed extraction
- `detail_level`
The default detail level is `minimal` for orientation, not full-page extraction; agents escalate detail or use `find` / `/observe` when they need more.

items.title: Executable acceptance oracles are absent from the assigned core
items.statement: The core provides many normative contracts and defaults but no named executable conformance tests, fixtures, receipts, or pass/fail oracle for dispatcher, WebAction, Site Reader, webfetch, LSP, or chatsearch behavior.
items.impact: Implementations cannot prove cross-adapter behavioral equivalence or canonical error/output conformance from this contract alone.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent test vectors and expected outcomes, especially around URL rejection, binary response shape, action validation, and search filtering.

dimension_assessments.summary: Core dispatcher, research, browser, fetch, LSP, and chatsearch behaviors are substantial, but WebAction field requirements and several branch choices remain unresolved.
Web and Site Reader capabilities are broad and bounded, while the LSP capability set is recommendation-level rather than an exact conformance floor.
Most input and output shapes are typed, but binary webfetch output, chatsearch bounds, WebAction action-specific fields, and detail vocabulary are incomplete or conflicting.
Locked registry, dispatcher, result, and audit contracts exist, with unresolved error-taxonomy and typed-output conflicts.
Research modes, cache states, and change statuses are named, but browser session state transitions and remediation completion are not defined.
PM registry authority, approval scope, and rename approval are explicit.
PM owns provider truth and Site Reader owns rendered page and session state.
Registry, GUI, audit, agent, and context-packer consumers are identified, but Context Lens permits two observably different consumer paths.
Support aliases, activity labels, prompt-injection chips, and degraded session explanation are specified, but session transition truth needed by GUI surfaces is incomplete.
Extraction, runtime degradation, iframe warnings, URL failures, and schema failures are explicit, but SSRF denial, robots exclusion, and session recovery contracts remain incomplete.
Credential references, scoped approvals, URL-scheme rejection, prompt-injection visibility, and chat secret scrubbing are covered; concrete SSRF/private-host enforcement is not.
Registry projections and audit vocabulary mappings propagate canonical truth, while muted-message propagation permits incompatible early-versus-late filtering.
Routing paths, cache TTLs, execution limits, activity labels, and audit fields support operations, but autonomous routing and robots defaults are discretionary.
Research, crawl, map, action timing, content size, iframe depth, and cache bounds are present; chatsearch k has no default or maximum.
Legacy names and shorthands are repeatedly normalized without creating new canonical families, and provider-specific vocabulary remains at adapter boundaries.
Normative expected behavior is rich, but no executable conformance oracle or fixture set is named in the assigned core.

Builders retain consequential choices in error mapping, SSRF enforcement, binary result shape, autonomous routing, robots behavior, session transitions, LSP floor, Context Lens filtering, chatsearch limits, WebAction validation, and detail vocabulary.

The most material ambiguities are unsupported-input taxonomy, SSRF defaults, metadata-only fetch output, state transitions, LSP normative strength, chatsearch filtering, action-field requirements, and detail-level mapping.
